messages:
jess_cs: FYI customer Meridian Market escalation — they say reranker quality dropped after the weekday rollout. Sent example queries and says top citation now unrelated. Customer says accuracy/regressions for product-safety and citation grounding.

mike_runtime: Can you paste one quick repro (query + expected vs actual) and the model/version + rollout id?

jess_cs: Sure — here's customer's minimal repro run they used:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "rdwr-rerank-v2",
  "reranker_version": "2.1.0",
  "query": "Does this jacket have waterproofing?",
  "candidates": ["doc:12345","doc:67890","doc:55512"]
}
```
Expected: doc:12345 (product spec) with grounding and citation.
Actual: doc:67890 (third-party blog) — low recall and wrong grounding.
They reported this started ~2026-11-03 03:15 UTC after rollout id 20261103-rerank-2.1.0 (canary 25%).

lucy_ml: Thanks. Do we know embedding/index versions? Reranker changes could cause score rescaling/feature shifts. Also did we update candidate generation or just ranking model?

jess_cs: Customer says embeddings = embeds-3.2. Index build ts: 2026-10-29T22:40Z. According to release notes the rollout included only reranker model weights and a normalization tweak (PR #8421) — canary target 25% (meridian account included).

infra-deploy-bot: deploy 20261103-rerank-2.1.0 started by mike_runtime at 2026-11-03T02:50:12Z — canary set for 25% — health checks passed.

eli_sre: Checked infra metrics for that window — latency and errors look normal. No OOMs or resource pressure on dedicated pools.

mike_runtime: OK. Lucy, can you run offline eval: run rerank-v2 vs rerank-v1 on the customer's query set (they sent ~120 queries). Also include nDCG and recall@1/3.

lucy_ml: Will queue. Also request: can jess share the customer's query file and sample golden doc IDs? Preferably minimal set of tokens used in repro.

jess_cs: Uploaded customer file to /shared/escalations/meridian_queries.csv and included mapping of expected doc ids. Also flagged high-priority. Customer is blocked in production; asked for ETA.

mike_runtime: Short term mitigation: switch Meridian's route to previous model (rdwr-rerank-v1) or bind them to dedicated A/B cohort. Should be a simple routing override — jess, want me to flip?

jess_cs: Please do — they'd accept short rollback while you investigate. Thanks :pray: 

mike_runtime: I'll open routing override ticket and enable v1 for meridian-account ID 67890. ETA 10m.

mike_runtime: done — routing override applied. Meridian now pinned to rdwr-rerank-v1. Please confirm with customer.

jess_cs: Confirmed — customer sees results back to expected baseline. They're relieved. Please keep me posted on root cause and next steps.

lucy_ml: Running offline eval now. Initial snapshot: ndcg@3 drop from 0.72 -> 0.61, recall@1 drop 0.55 -> 0.33 on their sample. Looks like re-scaling of dense scores vs BM25 features: PR #8421 changed score normalization. Investigating.

mike_runtime: If normalization tweak caused a weighted shift we can revert the normalization code-path and ship a patch. Lucy, how reproducible across other customers?

lucy_ml: Quick scan across sampled customers (10 corpora) shows small shifts but only Meridian's catalog is heavily dense-dominant — so regression amplified. Will prepare a short write-up and proposed revert.

jess_cs: Customer asked for permanent fix and wants rollback to be stable. They've asked for a postmortem and ETA for deploy of patch.

mike_runtime: I'll coordinate patch + canary with infra. Tentatively revert normalization in next hotfix and roll canary 10% -> monitor nDCG. Target timeline 6-8 hours.

eli_sre: Add alert to catch rerank nDCG delta > 0.05 for any account after rollout, and create playbook steps for routing overrides.

jess_cs: Thank you everyone — I'll update Meridian and set expectation. Will follow up with them after initial remediation.

lucy_ml: Put findings in thread: https://redwood.internal/esc-1234 (doc), will attach eval plots.

mike_runtime: Thanks — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
